questions.a: Jeanyoon Choi (최정윤, b. 1999) is a Korean computational artist and researcher who designs and researches multi-device web artworks about contemporary socio-technological systems, including AI, algorithmic culture and economic structures. He is a PhD candidate at KAIST's Experience Design Lab (XD Lab), advised by Dr. Yiyun Kang.

최정윤(Jeanyoon Choi, 1999년생)은 한국의 컴퓨테이셔널 아티스트이자 연구자로, AI, 알고리즘 문화, 경제 구조 등 동시대 사회기술 시스템의 복잡성을 다루는 멀티 디바이스 웹 아트워크를 만들고 연구합니다. 서울대학교 산업공학 학사, 영국 왕립예술학교(RCA) 정보경험디자인 석사를 마치고 현재 KAIST 경험디자인연구실(XD Lab) 박사과정에 있습니다.

questions.q: What is a multi-device web artwork?
questions.a: In Jeanyoon Choi's practice, a multi-device web artwork (MDWA) is an artwork built from internet-connected devices, typically audience members' own mobile phones linked to surrounding screens and projections, so that interaction on the phone changes the shared installation in real time. Examples include Banpo-Xism, Ω, SoTA and ≠ (Nonequality).

questions.q: What does Jeanyoon Choi research at KAIST?
questions.a: Jeanyoon Choi is a PhD candidate in Industrial Design at KAIST (Feb 2024 to Feb 2028) and a researcher in the Experience Design Lab directed by Dr. Yiyun Kang. His CV lists his research topics as Multi-Device Web Artwork, Computational Interactive Art, Complex Systems and Systems Art.

His CV lists selected exhibitions including Ars Electronica 2023 (Who Owns the Truth, Linz), Istanbul Digital Art Festival 2024 (Search Reality), Noli: jeux coréens at the Centre Culturel Coréen in Paris (2024), SoTA at KAIST Art Museum (2024-2025), Platform: Still Human at the KF XR Gallery in Seoul (2025-2026), Design Korea 2025 at COEX, the ACM DIS 2026 Interactivity Demo in Singapore and Living Geometry at YDP Art Square, Seoul (2026).

He is first author of 'SoTA: An Interactive Art Exhibition for Public AI Engagement' (ACM DIS 2026, Honourable Mention), co-author with Yiyun Kang of 'Passage of Water: Artistic Exploration of Earth's Freshwater with Google and NASA' (Leonardo, MIT Press, 2025, cover article), and co-author of 'Enumerating Multiplex Juggling Patterns' (Journal of Integer Sequences, 2019).

He received a BSc in Industrial Engineering from Seoul National University (2018-2022) and an MA in Information Experience Design from the Royal College of Art, London (2022-2023), and is a PhD candidate in Industrial Design at KAIST.

He was a lecturer at the Korea National University of Arts (K-Arts) Interaction Design Track from September 2024 to February 2026, teaching web-based experimental interaction design with Next.js, WebSocket and Three.js. He was also a teaching assistant for ID 412 Interactive Space and ID 430 Immersive Space at KAIST, and a front-end software engineering lecturer at Elice Coding in 2022.

questions.q: What themes does Jeanyoon Choi's art address?
questions.a: His works reflect the complexity of contemporary socio-technological systems, including AI, algorithmic culture and economic structures. Examples include South Korea's apartment hierarchy in Banpo-Xism, MBTI classification in Ω, neural network architectures in SoTA and the illogic of algorithmic outputs in ≠.

questions.q: What performances and talks has Jeanyoon Choi given?
questions.a: His CV lists performances including LING at The Place, London (2023), Counterpoint and Flicker at IKLECTIK, London (2023), IRCAM Forum events in Paris (2023) and Seoul (2024), and the lecture-performance 'Dadaism for the Algorithmic Age' at G-Artience, Daejeon (2024). Invited talks include artist talks at KAIST Art Museum (2024) and Living Geometry (2026), and a designer's talk at Design Korea 2025.

questions.q: What are Jeanyoon Choi's best-known artworks?
questions.a: His featured artworks are Banpo-Xism (2026) on Korean apartment culture, Ω (2025) on MBTI and algorithmic identity, SoTA (2024) on neural network architectures and explainable AI, and ≠ (Nonequality, 2023) on illogicality within logical systems. All four are multi-device web artworks.

terms.definition: Jeanyoon Choi's term for web-based artworks that interconnect audience mobile devices with surrounding screens and projections, creating interactive environments in which actions on personal phones change a shared installation.

A symphonic form of multi-device web artwork, introduced in The Symphony of Civilisation (2024), in which many connected channels and audience phones combine interactivity with collaborative immersion.
Jeanyoon Choi's minimalist approach to multi-device web artwork, presented in MBA (2022), that minimises external context and builds a work from consideration of the multi-device medium itself.
A term coined in the 2026 artwork of the same name for the Korean pursuit of one idealised real-estate coordinate of location and brand, a blind, zero-sum competition toward 'Banpo-Xi'.
